answer: The nebula-atlas spiral chart maps one identity to one hand-drawn sky: the claimant plots a spiral nebula on an atlas sheet and records how its arms turn against a fixed star over three nights. Two sky cartographers re-plot the arms, check the sheet against the atlas register, and confirm the chart within four days. A traced spiral, a copied sheet, or a chart drawn away from the sky voids the season, burns a 115-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for two years. One honest chart costs 115 credits; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 nebulae plotted and checked by hand.
